profile.title: Software Engineer | Java Backend Developer | DevOps Enthusiast | AI/ML Developer
introduction: I am a Computer Engineering student passionate about building scalable backend applications, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and AI-powered solutions.
My technical interests include Java, Spring Boot, Microservices, Python, Machine Learning, NLP, Docker, Kubernetes, and AWS.
I enjoy solving real-world engineering problems by developing applications that combine backend technologies, cloud infrastructure, and intelligent systems.
aboutText: I'm Abhijay Krishnan, a Computer Engineering student at NMIMS, Mumbai, passionate about building scalable software applications and intelligent systems.
My development journey includes building distributed payment processing systems, logistics platforms, NLP-based machine learning applications, and AI-powered tools.
I enjoy working across backend development, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, and artificial intelligence.
I am particularly interested in Java backend engineering, Spring Boot, microservices, distributed systems, and cloud technologies.
My goal is to become a strong software engineer capable of designing, developing, deploying, and maintaining scalable real-world applications.

payment-aiops-platform.title: Distributed Payment Processing & AI-Powered Self-Healing Platform
payment-aiops-platform.tagline: Four Spring Boot microservices move the money. A 13-stage multi-agent AIOps pipeline watches them, finds root causes and recommends recovery for a human to approve.
payment-aiops-platform.summary: A distributed payment processing platform built with Java 17, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and four REST microservices, containerised with Docker, deployed on Kubernetes and monitored with Prometheus, paired with an AI-powered incident response pipeline built in Python and LangGraph.
payment-aiops-platform.notes: Not fully autonomous: every recovery action recommended by the AIOps pipeline requires human approval before it is executed.

sections.heading: The Platform
sections.body: Developed a distributed payment processing platform using Java 17, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL and four REST microservices. The system uses JWT-based authentication and PostgreSQL for persistent data storage. The microservices are containerised using Docker and deployed on Kubernetes, with Prometheus monitoring.

sections.heading: The AIOps Layer
sections.body: Built a 13-stage multi-agent incident response pipeline using Python and LangGraph. The pipeline analyses incidents, retrieves historical context, identifies potential root causes and recommends recovery actions. Human approval is required before any recovery action is executed.

quickparcel.title: QuickParcel – Parcel Delivery Management Platform
quickparcel.tagline: A logistics platform connecting customers with vehicle providers: distance-based pricing, real routes on interactive maps, and synchronized dashboards.
quickparcel.summary: A parcel delivery and logistics platform that connects customers with vehicle providers. Customers enter pickup and destination locations, receive distance-based pricing estimates, find suitable vehicles and create parcel delivery bookings.
quickparcel.notes: QuickParcel is documented as two separate implementations: the version described in my resume uses Firebase Authentication and Firestore, while a separate Spring Boot + MySQL + Docker architecture was deployed on AWS EC2. They are not integrated with each other.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: QuickParcel connects customers with vehicle providers. Customers can enter pickup and destination locations, receive distance-based pricing estimates, find suitable vehicles, and create parcel delivery bookings.

sections.heading: Technical Implementation
sections.body: Developed Spring Boot REST APIs to handle booking, vehicle allocation, authentication, pricing, and user management. Integrated Leaflet and OSRM for route visualisation and distance calculation.

sections.heading: Implementation A: Resume Version
sections.body: The project version described in my resume uses Firebase services.

sections.heading: Implementation B: Containerised Deployment on AWS EC2
sections.body: A separate Spring Boot, MySQL and Docker-based architecture, deployed on AWS EC2 using Docker containers.
items: MySQL database container with persistent storage

sections.heading: Deployment Architecture
sections.body: OSRM is used as the external route calculation service.

fake-review-detection.title: Fake Review Detection System
fake-review-detection.tagline: Human or machine? An NLP system that separates genuine human-written reviews from AI-generated ones using classical ML, a BiLSTM and an ensemble.
fake-review-detection.summary: An NLP-based fake review detection system that classifies online product and service reviews as either human-written genuine reviews or AI-generated reviews produced by language models such as ChatGPT and GPT-4.
fake-review-detection.notes: All metrics are reported project results pending verification against the source code and evaluation files. The technologies listed span the project's experiments; not every model, dataset or library is part of a single production pipeline.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body: AI-generated reviews are increasingly used to manipulate online ratings and influence customer purchasing decisions. Traditional fake review detection systems focus on spam, duplicate reviews and suspicious user behaviour, but AI-generated reviews can be grammatically correct and resemble genuine human-written reviews.

sections.heading: The Approach
sections.body: The system classifies reviews into two categories, human-written genuine reviews and AI-generated reviews, by analysing linguistic patterns, vocabulary, sentiment, textual characteristics and contextual information.

sections.heading: NLP Preprocessing
sections.body: The project investigates and implements text preprocessing operations such as:

sections.heading: Deep Learning: Bidirectional LSTM
sections.body: Implemented a Bidirectional LSTM model for sequential text classification. The BiLSTM processes text in both forward and backward directions to capture contextual information.

sections.heading: Ensemble Learning
sections.body: The project combines Logistic Regression and BiLSTM predictions. The reported ensemble accuracy is achieved using a 0.5 decision threshold. An additional calibrated threshold of 0.22 reportedly produces 94.69% test accuracy while limiting false flags on genuine Amazon reviews to approximately 1%.

sections.heading: Longformer Integration
sections.body: The project also integrates a pretrained Longformer-based AI text detector, evaluated on additional AI-generated review sets (see Reported Results).

sections.heading: Datasets Investigated
sections.body: The exact datasets used by each training and evaluation pipeline are still to be verified against the source code.

currency-authentication.title: Currency Authentication System
currency-authentication.tagline: A machine learning counterfeit detector that analyses currency note images and classifies them through a real-time verification GUI.
currency-authentication.summary: A machine learning-based counterfeit currency detection system that uses image processing and classification techniques to analyse currency image characteristics and classify potentially genuine and counterfeit currency notes.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Built a machine learning-based counterfeit currency detection system using image processing and classification techniques. The system analyses currency image characteristics and uses machine learning models to classify potentially genuine and counterfeit currency notes.

sections.heading: Real-time Verification GUI
sections.body: Developed a real-time verification GUI using Tkinter.
